title: The $230M Question That Defines Cleveland's 2026 Season
thumb_prompt: A torn contract with $230M written in bold numbers burning at the edges, beside a quarterback helmet sitting on an empty stadium bench under harsh overhead lights, with shadows of two figures cast on the ground suggesting a difficult decision
thumb_subject: a determined quarterback in an orange and brown number four jersey holding a football under stadium lights

sections.heading: The Weight of a Guaranteed Contract

paragraphs.text: Eleven days until kickoff in Chicago. Eleven days until the Cleveland Browns take the field for their first preseason game. And after all the practices, all the joint sessions, all the reps, we still do not have an answer to the most important question facing this franchise. Who is the starting quarterback? But here is the thing nobody wants to say out loud. This might not actually be a football decision. <cite index="35-1,35-2">Deshaun Watson carries a forty six million dollar base salary this season</cite>. That is not a typo. Forty six million reasons why this quarterback competition might already be decided before Todd Monken ever announces a starter.

<cite index="37-5,37-6">Watson has played just nineteen games for Cleveland since the blockbuster trade in March twenty twenty two</cite>. <cite index="37-6">He tore his Achilles on October twentieth twenty twenty four, then tore it again requiring a second surgery in January twenty twenty five</cite>. He missed all of last season. Two years removed from the field. And yet, <cite index="36-7,36-8,36-9">Browns insider Tony Grossi believes the job is Watson's to lose</cite>. That tells you everything about how much that contract weighs on every decision this organization makes. The Browns cannot escape it. They are financially handcuffed to a player who has not looked like a franchise quarterback since he wore a Texans uniform.

And then there is Shedeur Sanders. The fall heard around the football world. <cite index="55-1,55-2">Projected as a first round lock by many analysts, Sanders tumbled all the way to pick one forty four in the fifth round</cite>. <cite index="56-6">Five other quarterbacks were selected ahead of him</cite>. Character concerns. Commitment questions. <cite index="57-9,57-10">League insiders wondered if he was totally committed to being a great quarterback</cite>. But the talent is undeniable. <cite index="61-7">He broke over one hundred school records at Colorado, including single season passing yards and completion percentage</cite>. The Browns traded up to get him. That means something. You do not trade draft capital for a guy you view as a backup project. Cleveland saw value where thirty one other teams passed.
card_lines: Fell from 1st round projection to pick 144
Browns traded up to secure him

paragraphs.text: <cite index="38-6,38-7">Monken revealed Watson and Sanders will each get one start in the first two preseason games</cite>. <cite index="5-7">The first preseason game is August fifteenth at Chicago</cite>. That is the evaluation window. That is where this gets decided. Or does it? Because here is what makes this entire situation so maddening for Browns fans. <cite index="3-3">Watson threw back to back interceptions to Denzel Ward and Damarri Mathis in eleven on eleven drills on day one of camp</cite>. Meanwhile, <cite index="3-10,3-12,3-13,3-14">Sanders ended practice with the number two offense by connecting with Gage Larvadain on a deep touchdown to finish a two minute drill, after finding Tylan Wallace on a back shoulder fade and hitting rookie KC Concepcion for an earlier touchdown</cite>. The gap in performance has been visible. And yet, the money talks louder.

Let me take you back to another franchise quarterback decision that haunted a team. The Browns in nineteen ninety nine, coming back from the expansion draft. They took Tim Couch first overall. Gave him the keys immediately. But the offensive line was not ready. The weapons were not there. Couch took a beating physically and mentally. His career never recovered from being rushed into action before the supporting cast was built. That is the cautionary tale hanging over the Shedeur Sanders discussion. <cite index="41-2,41-3,41-4">Some believe Watson, who has been better at presnap activities, could help the young core of players develop by getting the process right, making the right audibles, sliding protections, and getting plays off in time</cite>. If the quarterback cannot handle those responsibilities, young players could learn bad habits and see their development set back. There is an argument for patience with Sanders. But is it the right one?

<cite index="45-1">On June second, the Browns traded reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for Jared Verse and multiple draft picks</cite>. <cite index="46-3">Cleveland received a first round pick in twenty twenty seven, a second rounder in twenty twenty eight, and a third in twenty twenty nine</cite>. The best player in modern Browns history. Gone. <cite index="45-11">Andrew Berry said their goal was for Garrett to be a one helmet player for his entire career</cite>. And then they shipped him out. <cite index="46-11">Garrett had a rare no trade clause in his four year, one hundred sixty million dollar contract</cite>. He waived it to go chase a championship in Los Angeles. That tells you what he thought about Cleveland's timeline. This is a rebuild disguised as a retool.

<cite index="47-6,47-7">The Rams acquired one of the most dominant edge rushers of the twenty first century, a player who broke the NFL single season sack record in twenty twenty five with one hundred twenty five point five career sacks</cite>. Meanwhile, <cite index="49-12">Verse has collected twelve sacks, seventy one tackles, and five forced fumbles in two seasons since being drafted nineteenth overall in twenty twenty four</cite>. The production gap is massive. <cite index="49-14">Garrett has thirty seven sacks to Verse's twelve over the last two years</cite>. But Verse is twenty five years old with two Pro Bowls already. <cite index="49-9">From Dayton, Ohio, he returns home</cite>. And <cite index="49-2,49-3,49-4,49-5">Verse has already been coaching up rookie tackle Spencer Fano after beating him on an up and under move, staying after practice to walk him through leverage and technique</cite>. That is leadership. That is culture building.
card_lines: Garrett: 125.5 career sacks, 37 in last 2 years
Verse: 12 sacks, 2 Pro Bowls in 2 seasons
Verse age 25, Ohio native returns home

paragraphs.text: Jared Verse is not Myles Garrett. Not yet. Maybe not ever. But that is not the point of this trade. Cleveland is stockpiling draft capital for the future. They are betting on their ability to develop young talent. <cite index="15-1,15-6">The roster includes fifty four players aged twenty five and under, led by linebacker Carson Schwesinger and edge rusher Verse</cite>. <cite index="15-5">Twenty three rookies are on the ninety man training camp roster, including ten draft picks from twenty twenty six</cite>. This is about twenty twenty seven and twenty twenty eight. About building something sustainable instead of chasing one more mediocre season with aging stars and an expensive quarterback who cannot stay healthy. The Garrett trade was an admission. An acceptance of reality. This team is not winning now. So why mortgage the future pretending otherwise?

<cite index="17-2,17-3">Cleveland also lost defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz, who resigned after being passed over for the head coaching job in favor of Monken, with Mike Rutenberg stepping in as first time defensive coordinator</cite>. <cite index="17-4">Rutenberg says he is keeping the defensive scheme intact but will incorporate his own flavor</cite>. New coordinator. New defensive anchor. <cite index="16-13,16-14">Verse joins defensive ends Alex Wright and Isaiah McGuire plus second year defensive tackle Mason Graham</cite>. <cite index="28-1">Graham was one of the blue chip prospects at interior defensive tackle, paired with free agent signee Maliek Collins</cite>. The pieces are intriguing. The potential is real. But can a first time coordinator replace one of the best defensive minds in football while also replacing the best pass rusher in franchise history? That is asking a lot. That is asking everything.
card_lines: Jim Schwartz resigned after HC snub
New system, new star, high expectations

paragraphs.text: <cite index="4-6">Before practice on day eleven, Monken announced he promoted two players to the first string offense: left tackle Spencer Fano and wide receiver Denzel Boston</cite>. <cite index="4-7">Fano seems to have won favor by not being intimidated by defensive end Jared Verse on Saturday</cite>. The ninth overall pick in this year's draft just got bumped up to protect Watson or Sanders or whoever ends up taking snaps in week one. <cite index="13-10,13-11">Boston, the number thirty nine pick out of Washington, gives Cleveland a size dimension at six foot four and two hundred fifteen pounds that the offense lacked last season, and has been working with the second team offense but is expected to have a big role as a rookie</cite>. These promotions matter because they signal what Monken values. Fano standing his ground against Verse. Boston making plays consistently. Earn it and you will play. That is the culture shift.

<cite index="4-8">In a corresponding move, Monken envisions wide receiver Jerry Jeudy being moved around a lot, since they feel he is better on the move</cite>. Jeudy came over in a trade and has NFL experience. But the rookies are pushing. That is what you want to see. <cite index="13-7,13-8">Boston had one of the catches of camp, leaping over a defensive back along the sideline to bring in a pass from Shedeur Sanders in seven on seven drills</cite>. <cite index="10-16,10-17">The Browns revamped their wide receiver room, drafting Boston and KC Concepcion</cite>. <cite index="17-1">Second year player Isaiah Bond was a standout in the spring and could have a bigger role in twenty twenty six</cite>. Depth at receiver has been a problem in Cleveland for years. They are trying to fix it by going young and hungry. The chemistry between Sanders and these receivers has been visible in camp. That connection matters.
card_lines: Isaiah Bond poised for bigger role

paragraphs.text: <cite index="16-1,16-2,16-3">On offense, a revamped offensive line is highlighted by tackle Tytus Howard, acquired in a trade from the Texans, along with free agents Elgton Jenkins and Zion Johnson, joining ninth overall pick Spencer Fano</cite>. <cite index="19-20">Cleveland released tackle Jack Conklin, tight end David Njoku, and guard Wyatt Teller this offseason</cite>. That is three established starters gone. Three new faces in. <cite index="14-8,14-9">The biggest question is whether Elgton Jenkins or Teven Jenkins will be at right guard, with Elgton potentially at center and Teven at guard</cite>. This offensive line could have five new starters from last season. Five guys learning to play together while protecting a quarterback who has not played in two years or a rookie who is learning NFL speed. The margin for error is razor thin. One injury and this whole thing falls apart.

<cite index="20-1,20-3,20-4">The Browns claimed defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins off waivers from the Jets on August seventh due to a rash of injuries at the position</cite>. <cite index="13-2,13-3">Guard Zak Zinter left practice on a cart, and sixteen players did not practice Thursday including Mason Graham, Elgton Jenkins, and Teven Jenkins</cite>. The injury bug is already biting in August. Training camp attrition is real every year. But when you are this young, this inexperienced, this reliant on rookies and new additions, losing bodies in camp creates chaos. Depth is being tested before the games even start. <cite index="21-2,21-3">First round pick KC Concepcion seemed to injure his shoulder on Monday</cite>. If he misses time, that is a huge blow to an offense counting on him to contribute immediately. Every practice rep matters when you are installing a new system.

<cite index="6-1,6-11">There is very little optimism around the league regarding the Browns current quarterback competition</cite>. <cite index="6-3,6-13">Rival coaches and executives were not very nice when discussing Shedeur Sanders</cite>. That is the league talking. That is what other teams think when they look at Cleveland's quarterback room. No hope. No upside. A washed veteran on a bloated contract and a fifth round rookie with character questions. <cite index="42-5">Sanders had an average time to throw of three point two four seconds, the longest of thirty eight quarterbacks who made at least six starts in twenty twenty five</cite>. He holds the ball too long. That gets you killed in the NFL, especially behind a rebuilt offensive line. These are the red flags that made him fall in the draft. These are the concerns that will not just disappear because he is in the pros now.
card_lines: Little league optimism for Browns QBs

paragraphs.text: But here is what nobody expected. <cite index="13-4,13-5,13-6">Watson had a slow start to training camp but had his best day to date on Wednesday, throwing multiple touchdowns and looking more in sync and confident pushing the ball downfield</cite>. <cite index="42-1,42-2,42-3,42-4">Monken said Watson's athleticism shows up, that he has had injuries that set him back, and that his athleticism is one of his superpowers</cite>. If Watson looks healthy, truly healthy for the first time since that Achilles rupture, this conversation shifts. Suddenly the money makes sense. Suddenly starting him is not just about the contract, it is about giving the team the best chance to win. That would be the dream scenario for Cleveland. The reality? We will not know until those preseason lights come on and Watson takes real hits from real pass rushers trying to separate him from the football.

<cite index="3-8,3-9">Veteran defensive end Jadeveon Clowney visited the Browns on Wednesday, having had a two year stint in Cleveland from twenty twenty one to twenty twenty two and recording eleven sacks</cite>. But <cite index="21-2,21-3,22-1,22-6">a day after being spurned by Clowney, Andrew Berry added defensive tackle Travis Bell to the roster and waived undrafted free agent running back TJ Harden</cite>. Clowney said no to coming back. That hurts. He saw this roster and said no thanks. That is a message. That is a veteran pass rusher who knows what it takes to win looking at Cleveland and deciding he would rather wait for another opportunity. You cannot ignore that. You cannot spin that into a positive. The Browns are not an attractive destination right now. Free agents are not lining up to come here. That makes every draft pick more important. That makes player development everything.

Here is the uncomfortable truth about this season. <cite index="35-6,35-7">Many believe Cleveland is focused on twenty twenty seven as they look for their franchise quarterback in next year's draft, which is why some argue Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for twenty twenty six</cite>. <cite index="9-7,9-9">Owner Jimmy Haslam and GM Andrew Berry were spotted on the sidelines of the Texas season opener, fueling rumors that Haslam has his eyes on Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning, who came into the season as the presumed top prospect in the twenty twenty six class</cite>. If that is true, if Cleveland is already looking past this season to next year's draft, then what is the point of starting Watson? Give Sanders the reps. Let him take his lumps. See what you have. Because if he is not the answer, you need to know that before you are staring at another top ten pick in April twenty twenty seven trying to decide between quarterbacks again.

<cite index="7-1,7-4">The Browns traded Myles Garrett, but their actions continue to show they are committed to competing in twenty twenty six</cite>. But are they really? Competing means going into the season believing you can make the playoffs. Believing you can win the division. Does anyone actually believe that about these Browns? <cite index="51-1">Cleveland is trying to improve on their five and twelve record from twenty twenty five, return to the playoffs after a two year absence, and end their thirty three season division title drought, having last won the then AFC Central in nineteen eighty nine</cite>. Thirty three years. Three decades without winning the division. That is generational suffering. That is fathers passing disappointment down to sons. And this roster is supposed to break that streak? With a quarterback competition that might come down to money instead of merit?

The first preseason game is August fifteenth against Chicago. That is four days away. Four days until we start getting real answers about who this team is. <cite index="10-13,10-14,10-15">Cleveland will host Buffalo for a joint practice on August twentieth before their second preseason game at home against the Bills on August twenty second, then wrap up the preseason hosting the Patriots on August twenty seventh</cite>. <cite index="16-12">The Browns will kick off the regular season on September thirteenth by going on the road to face the Jaguars</cite>. Jacksonville. A team that also traded for a Browns cornerback this offseason. A team that also is trying to figure out what they are. That week one game will tell us everything about whether Cleveland took steps forward or if this is going to be another long winter in Ohio.

This is not about one season. This is about the next five years of Browns football. <cite index="35-13">The Browns agreed to make Watson's two hundred thirty million dollar contract fully guaranteed back in twenty twenty two</cite>. That decision will define this franchise for the rest of the decade. You cannot undo it. You cannot trade him. You cannot cut him without destroying your salary cap. You are stuck. And so the question becomes, do you lean into the mistake and start him because of the money, or do you pivot to the future and give Sanders every chance to prove he can be the guy? There is no easy answer. There is no right answer. There is only the answer that Andrew Berry and Todd Monken believe gives them the best chance to keep their jobs. And that answer might have nothing to do with winning football games in twenty twenty six.
card_lines: No easy escape from Watson deal

paragraphs.text: I keep coming back to that forty six million dollar number. That is more than some teams spend on their entire offense. That is generational wealth for one player who has not proven he can stay healthy, who has not proven he can win in Cleveland, who has not played meaningful football in two years. But it is guaranteed. Every single penny. So what do you do? You start him. You hope he can recapture something. You hope the offensive line holds up. You hope the weapons are good enough. You hope the defense can carry this team while Watson shakes off the rust. And if it does not work? If Watson struggles or gets hurt again? Then you have your answer. Then you turn to Sanders and you do not look back. That is the path. That is the reality. The two hundred thirty million dollar question will be answered one way or another this season. And the Browns better hope they can live with the answer.
